name: acad-styles
description: Authoring the styles a drawing is held to: dimension styles, multileader styles and table styles, with the same properties-map shape for all three, so a caller who has learned one has learned the others. Create with chosen properties, change one, duplicate a dimension style for another scale, delete, or make current. Properties are named plainly - textHeight, arrowSize, dataTextHeight - not API spellings, and the list_*_properties tools report every name, the variable behind it, what it does and its range. Table text heights are per row, because a schedule's caption, headings and content are three different sizes.

tools_summary.name: copy_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Duplicate a dimension style under a new name, optionally overriding some properties in the same call. This is how a 1:100 style is made from a 1:50 one: copy it, override scale, done - and the two changes stay atomic instead of leaving a half-made style behind if the second call fails.

tools_summary.name: create_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Create a named dimension style with chosen properties - text height, arrow size, decimal places, overall scale and the rest. Pass properties as a name-to-value map; use list_dimstyle_properties for the names and ranges. An unknown property name or an out-of-range value is an error, never silently skipped, because skipping would report success over a style that is not what was asked for. Refuses an existing name unless overwrite is true.

tools_summary.name: create_mleaderstyle
tools_summary.description: Create a named multileader style with chosen properties - text height, arrow size, dogleg length, whether the leader has a landing, how many points it may have. Pass properties as a name-to-value map; an unknown name or an out-of-range value is an error rather than a silent skip. Refuses an existing name unless overwrite is true.
intent: new leader style with 2.5 mm text

tools_summary.name: create_tablestyle
tools_summary.description: Create a named table style with chosen properties - cell margins, flow direction, and text height per row type. This is what makes a generated door or room schedule match the rest of the set instead of arriving at AutoCAD's defaults. Refuses an existing name unless overwrite is true.

tools_summary.name: delete_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Delete a dimension style. Refuses to delete 'Standard', refuses to delete the current style, and refuses a style still in use - with the reason, and a pointer to dimensions.set_entity_dimstyle for moving the dimensions off it first.

tools_summary.name: delete_mleaderstyle
tools_summary.description: Delete a multileader style. Refuses to delete 'Standard', refuses to delete the current style, and refuses one still in use - with the reason rather than a bare AutoCAD error code.

tools_summary.name: delete_tablestyle
tools_summary.description: Delete a table style. Refuses to delete 'Standard', refuses to delete the current style, and refuses one still in use - with the reason rather than a bare AutoCAD error code.

tools_summary.name: list_dimstyle_properties
tools_summary.description: List every dimension-style property this bank can set, with the AutoCAD DIMVAR behind it, what it does, and its valid range. Read-only. Call this first: the property names here are plain (textHeight, arrowSize, decimalPlaces) rather than DIMVAR spellings, because nobody should have to know that a text height is called DIMTXT in order to set one.

tools_summary.name: list_mleaderstyle_properties
tools_summary.description: List every multileader-style property this bank can set, with the API member behind it, what it does and its valid range. Read-only. Booleans travel as 0 or 1 so the whole properties argument stays one map of names to numbers - two value types in one dictionary would be two ways to be wrong about it.

tools_summary.name: list_mleaderstyles
tools_summary.description: List the multileader styles defined in this drawing with all their properties, and which one is current. Read-only.

tools_summary.name: list_tablestyle_properties
tools_summary.description: List every table-style property this bank can set, with the API member behind it, which row it applies to, what it does and its range. Read-only. Text heights are per row - titleTextHeight, headerTextHeight, dataTextHeight - because a schedule's caption, its column headings and its content are three different sizes and pretending otherwise is how tables end up unreadable.

tools_summary.name: list_tablestyles
tools_summary.description: List the table styles defined in this drawing with all their properties, and which one is current. Read-only. The schedules family draws into whichever style is current, so this is what tells you what a generated door or room schedule will look like before you generate it.

tools_summary.name: modify_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Change properties on an existing dimension style, leaving the rest alone. The stored style changes immediately; dimensions already placed pick it up on the next regen, and the result says so - an unchanged screen after this call is not a failed call.

tools_summary.name: modify_mleaderstyle
tools_summary.description: Change properties on an existing multileader style, leaving the rest alone. The stored style changes immediately; multileaders already placed pick it up on the next regen, and the result says so.

tools_summary.name: modify_tablestyle
tools_summary.description: Change properties on an existing table style, leaving the rest alone. The stored style changes immediately; tables already placed pick it up on the next regen, and the result says so.

tools_summary.name: set_current_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Make a dimension style the current one, so dimensions placed afterwards use it. Returns the style with all its properties, so the caller can confirm what they just switched to rather than trusting the name.

tools_summary.name: set_current_mleaderstyle
tools_summary.description: Make a multileader style the current one, so leaders placed afterwards use it. Returns the style with all its properties, so the caller can confirm what they switched to rather than trusting the name.

tools_summary.name: set_current_tablestyle
tools_summary.description: Make a table style the current one, so tables created afterwards use it - including the ones the schedules family generates. Returns the style with all its properties so the caller can confirm what they switched to.
